feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed. I kept the iteration 5 controller unchanged (kp 3.5, kd 0.5, ki 0.05, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]), because the wheel radius does not change the steering equation, and the radius change is then the only variable. Evidence: iteration 4 (radius 0.035 to 0.040 m) lifted oval finish from 65% to 80%, and iteration 5 (mass 0.5 kg) lifted it to 95% with oval mean time 1.71 s, so there is margin to spend on speed. Iteration 6 (0.4 kg) and iteration 7 (track 0.09 m) both lowered performance, so do not move mass or track further down. Depending on the next race: if oval finish holds at 95% or more and s-bend off-track exits do not rise, keep radius 0.045 m and move to 0.050 m, the contract limit. If oval finish falls or s-bend and slalom off-track exits rise while max_error stays near 0.06 m, speed is outrunning steering, so return to radius 0.040 m and widen wheel_track to 0.11 m for yaw stability. This widening is an untested hypothesis, reasoned from iteration 7, where narrowing the track to 0.09 m raised oscillation and cut oval finish to 60%. If slalom line losses stay near 1.85 with the radius change alone, the slalom limit is sensor coverage, not speed.
requested_changes: If oval finish rate holds at 95% or more with no rise in s-bend off-track exits, raise wheel_radius from 0.045 to 0.050 m (the contract maximum). Iteration 4 showed radius 0.035 to 0.040 m lifted oval finish from 65% to 80%, and iteration 5 kept it at 95%, so speed is still paying off.

If oval finish or s-bend progress falls while max_error stays near 0.06 m, return wheel_radius to 0.040 m and try wheel_track 0.11 m for more yaw stability. This is untested: iteration 7 showed that narrowing the track to 0.09 m hurt oval finish (95% to 60%), so widening it is the reverse, reasoned step.

If the radius change holds oval finish, retest the outer spread at radius 0.045 m: x = ±0.045 m at y=0.07 m with 16 mm footprints. Iteration 8 showed this spread cut slalom line losses from 1.85 to 1.0, but the oval fell to 65% at radius 0.040 m, so the extra speed may now absorb the cost.
